title: RescueSpeech: A German Corpus for Speech Recognition in Search and Rescue Domain
why_promising: Primary German speech recorded in simulated search-and-rescue exercises; Zenodo explicitly states that the recordings are manually annotated and provides 2,412 clean ASR utterances (1 h 36 min) with open archive files and MD5 checksums. This is primary non-singing production and potentially useful for utterance/word-level timing, task/style, speaker and acoustic-context metadata.
open_question: Before core admission, inspect the ASR archive internals and README to establish annotation granularity (transcript-only versus time-aligned word/segment labels), verify whether annotation boundaries/labels themselves were manually created or exhaustively human-verified, and record exact license/redistribution terms. Synthetic noisy derivatives must be lineage-linked and excluded from unique primary-production counts.
